text:
A: Hi, can you hear me alright?
B: Yes, thank you. Hello. I'm Imran, I'm in Huddersfield.
A: Gareth, Chelmsford. Nice to meet you. What do you do, Imran?
B: Er, IT support. Part-time. I look after an accountancy firm and a dental practice. Their laptops, backups, Microsoft 365, that sort of thing.
A: Freelance, then? Your own clients?
B: Sort of, yes. It's all word of mouth, really. I've been thinking about setting up properly as a sole trader, with a website and so on, but I keep putting it off. I'm not very good at, you know, selling myself.
A: Honestly, that's the bit most people struggle with. I'm in sales, more or less. I'm a travel consultant, high-end tailor-made trips. And the thing I'd say is, you don't need to be pushy. You just need three or four happy clients saying your name in the right rooms. The website's almost secondary. Get a couple of testimonials up, a clear list of what you do, and a price range so people aren't scared off. Keep it simple, yeah?
B: That's helpful, actually. The dentist would probably give me a nice quote. Their printer's terrible, so I'm there a lot.
A: There you go. Free marketing, that printer.
B: Ha, I suppose so. Do you enjoy it, the travel?
A: I love it. I've just been to Japan again, my fifth time. I go on fam trips, which is basically the hotels and tourism boards hosting agents so we can sell them properly. Hard life, I know.
B: That sounds very nice. I'm not a big flyer, to be honest. I get a bit anxious about connections.
A: You're not alone. Where have you been?
B: Pakistan, a few times, for family. And I did Umrah with my mum in 2019. That was... that was very special. She passed the year after, so.
A: Oh, I'm sorry. That must make it mean a lot more now.
B: It does. Thank you. Otherwise, I prefer the Lakes, the Dales, Whitby. I print the itinerary out and book the parking before we go. My partner laughs at me.
A: Don't let her. That's literally what people pay me for. Printed itinerary, booked parking. You'd be my favourite client.
B: Ha. Is that alright, though? I always feel I'm overdoing it.
A: No, it's smart. I leave a day or two blank on mine, mind, just to wander, but the rest is in a spreadsheet.
B: I've got spreadsheets for everything too. Each client has a log.
A: See, that's a selling point. Put that on your website. "Everything documented." Small businesses love that, to be honest. What do you do to switch off?
B: Cricket, mostly. Yorkshire. I used to play in the Huddersfield league. Now I watch with my son.
A: I'm more Formula One. And running, I'm training for a marathon.
B: Oh, I walk a lot. Castle Hill, the canal. Step count, mostly.
A: Same instinct, really. Logging everything. What's your daily target?
B: Twelve thousand. On a good day. Wednesdays I do less, because the kids come for tea and I'm...
